name: Spitalfields City Farm
summary: A city farm on Buxton Street, started in 1978 on a former railway goods depot. It describes itself as the closest city farm to the Square Mile.
crowd: Says its purpose is a welcoming city farm linking people of every age and culture with food, animals and nature.

accessibility.notes: Euan's Guide, with details supplied by the farm, says the gardens and farmyard are accessible though some pathways may be difficult, with ramps to the picnic areas, shop, office and several other buildings. Disabled parking is available by prior arrangement. Assistance dogs are welcome.

cost.notes: Visits are free; the farm also holds ticketed activities and after-hours events.

evidence.quote: Sited on a former railway goods depot, the Farm was started in 1978 in response to local people’s wishes
Spitalfields City Farm is the nearest city farm to the City of London’s square mile.
Our Purpose is to sustain and develop a welcoming city farm that connects people of all ages and culture to food, animals and nature.
1 disabled toilet with large doorway and hand rails
Gardens and Farmyard accessible but may have difficulties on some pathways
Ramps to picnic areas, shop, office, yurt, tent, and eco-station.
Disabled parking available with prior arrangement. Please call the office to confirm : 0207 247 8762
We are happy to welcome Guide Dogs for the Blind, Disability Assistance Dogs
Plan your FREE visit to Spitalfields City Farm
We host special activities and after hour ticketed events.
Spitalfields City Farm, Buxton Street, London E1 5AR
